official2027ProductPage.title: K2 Passport Unisex Snowboard 2027
official2027ProductPage.hostNote: K2 official US storefront. Listed price is regional US USD and does not establish China-market pricing.
official2027ProductPage.evidence: Confirms SKU KB261689, 2027 model, current US listed price USD 599.95, 13 lengths, Directional Combination Camber, Tapered Directional / Traditional Shape, A1 Core, ICG 10 Triax Glass with Carbon, and Sintered 4000 Stone Finish Base. theGoodRide.title: K2 Passport 2023-2024 Snowboard Review
theGoodRide.hostNote: Historical model-year review, not a 2027 sample. Its test block discloses an extended demo but does not date the physical sample separately; summary notes the product had not changed for the 2024 update.
theGoodRide.testSetup: Size 157; four days; firm to good mid-winter snow at Mission Ridge, mixed spring conditions and 6 inches of spring powder; reviewer boot US 9, height 5 ft 10 in, weight 185-190 lb.
theGoodRide.evidence: Reports a damp/rubbery medium-to-medium-stiff ride, quick edge transitions and tighter turns, competent but not specialist hard-snow hold, easy skidded turns, strong all-condition consistency, moderate directional float (reviewer did not stress-test it in powder), usable switch, pipe and jumps, but a less stable jump platform than some boards and only average jibbing. Exact board mass intentionally not published; it only felt normal.

snowboardingProfiles.title: K2 Passport Snowboard Review
snowboardingProfiles.hostNote: Historical review sample is explicitly a 2024 size 160 board tested 2024-01-23, not a 2027 test. Its 85.6/100 overall score and category scores use the site's own composite rubric and are not mapped to this project's six editorial dimensions.
snowboardingProfiles.evidence: Directional observations describe damp stability in messy conditions, competent firm-snow grip and carving, but physical effort for some turns; powder assessment is inferred from shape/specs rather than a powder-day test, and jump pop is average. This is historical directional context only.

units.effectiveEdgeCm: Official table unit cm; converted to mm for seed sizeSpecs.
units.noseWaistTailCm: Official table order nose/waist/tail and unit cm; each converted to mm for seed sizeSpecs.
units.sidecutRadiiM: Official table gives three radii in source order; no heel/toe labels are supplied, so none are inferred.
units.referenceStanceInches: One reference stance, not a selectable stance range; source value is retained exactly and converted to nearest mm for display.
units.setbackInches: Official table lists 0.75 in for every size. Seed uses positive magnitude 19 mm (rounded from 19.05 mm), matching existing K2 seed convention; direction is tailward for this directional board.
units.riderWeight: K2 publishes recommended lb and kg ranges per size; source strings retained verbatim below.

representativeSize.basis: Median of seven standard sizes [146,149,151,154,157,160,163]; wide variants are excluded. The 157 official geometry row is directly listed, not interpolated.

officialUS.priceType: official US storefront listed price; not expressly labeled MSRP
officialUS.note: Dynamic regional listing, not a verified China-market price.

seed.note: Project currency normalization only, not a Chinese retail offer; value score remains low confidence until local price evidence is available.

theGoodRide.conditions: Firm to good Mission Ridge mid-winter snow, mixed spring conditions and 6 inches of spring powder.

observations.stability: Damp and consistent across tried conditions; hard-snow hold was competent, not specialist.
observations.response: Fast edge-to-edge and prefers tighter turns; easy to skid and reasonably forgiving.
observations.float: Some powder exposure but explicitly not stress-tested; reviewer describes a useful one-board directional float, not a dedicated-powder choice.
observations.park: Usable for pipe/jumps; reviewer notes a less stable jump platform than some and average jibbing.
observations.forgiveness: Less catchy than profile suggests and easy to skid; medium-to-medium-stiff feel.
observations.value: Reviewer says glide is middle ground, neither especially fast nor slow; this does not establish China-market value.

snowboardingProfiles.observations: Damp/stable in messy conditions, capable carving and firm-snow edge hold; some turns take physical effort. Powder is inferred from shape/specs, not directly tested; jump pop is average. Historical supporting context only.

scoringEvidence.siteScoreDecision: Keep existing stability 7.9 / response 8.1 / float 7.0 / park 6.5 / forgiveness 7.6 / value 7.1 as low-to-moderate-confidence editorial estimates. The 2023-24 disclosed test generally supports a damp, quick-turning, relatively forgiving all-mountain freeride character, but its limited powder exposure and non-2027 sample do not justify precise numeric remapping. Park remains a modest all-around estimate, not a park specialization. Value is least reliable: the US USD 599.95 and official Japan JPY 84,700 tax-inclusive prices are regional references only; seed CNY 4320 normalizes the US listing using the project's 7.2 rate, not a verified local price. Do not map external composites/category ratings to the project's six axes.
scoringEvidence.confidence: moderate for broad ride direction based on historical disclosed four-day test; low for exact 2027 performance, powder/park scores and local value

seedMappingNotes: Official source publishes 13 sizes; YAML sizeSpecs contains every row. Standard sizes are 146/149/151/154/157/160/163; 157 is their median. Wide rows remain explicitly tagged.
Official triple sidecut radii are preserved in source order; no heel/toe interpretation is invented.
K2's Stance column is a single reference width, not a stance range. The table setback is 0.75 in; the seed uses a positive rounded 19 mm magnitude per existing K2 convention.
No official board mass was located. The Good Ride only gives a subjective 'normal' impression and intentionally does not publish exact mass; no numerical weight is inferred.
No China-market price or verified third-party image reuse license was found.
